title: 2002 AMC 10B Problem 3
statement: The arithmetic mean of the nine numbers in the set \(\{9, 99, 999, 9999, \ldots, 999999999\}\) is a \(9\)-digit number \(M,\) all of whose digits are distinct. Which digit does the number \(M\) not contain?

solutions.text:
The mean is \[ \begin{aligned} &\dfrac{1}{9} \\ &\quad {}\cdot \small \left(9 + 99 + 999 + \cdots + 999999999\right) \\ &= 1 + 11 + 111 + \cdots \\ &\quad {}+ 111111111. \end{aligned} \]

Adding these nine repunits column by column gives \(M = 123456789.\)

The only digit missing from \(M\) is \(0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Each term is \(9\) times a repunit, so divide the sum by \(9\) first
